content: === Introduction ===

Joubert is a French surname. It is a regional variant form of Jaubert, originating in the centre west and centre south of France.[1] This surname is common in South Africa and Namibia, particularly among the descendants of Huguenot settlers.
It may refer to:
=== Persons ===
<info> Barthelemy Catherine Joubert (1769–1799), French general during the French Revolutionary Wars
<info> Christiaan Johannes Joubert (1834–1911), South African soldier, politician and vice president of the South African Republic
<info> David Joubert, South African general, nephew of Petrus Jacobus "Piet" Joubert
<info> Léopold Louis Joubert (1842–1927), French soldier and lay missionary in the Belgian Congo
<info> Piet Joubert (1831–1900), South African commandant-general (equivalent to major general) and vice president of the South African Republic
<info> Philip Joubert de la Ferté, British air marshal
<info> John Joubert (composer) (1927–2019), British composer
<info> The Joubert Singers, choir, notable for "Stand on the Word"
<info> Phyliss McKoy-Joubert, composer, most notably for "Stand on the Word"
<info> Gwynneth Joubert, South African singer-songwriter, known by her stage name as Gwynneth Ashley-Robin, most notably for Little Jimmy and Little Soldier Blue
<info> André Joubert (born 1964), South African rugby union player
<info> Brian Joubert (born 1984), French figure skater

<info> John Joubert (serial killer) (1963–1996), American serial killer
